note: Track keys, step 3: the flat keys after F, found anticlockwise on the circle, each one's new flat ringed on its 4th note on three staffs side by side (the keys are the lesson, so they are written out, not a Key selector or moves), then all four flats counted on the piano in A♭ major. Each section has a feel to reach.

exercise.title: The flat keys, the other way round
exercise.why: Each key a 5th down keeps the flats of the key before it and adds one more, on its 4th note, so the circle gives the flat keys in order the other way round.

cells.text:
The circle below starts on F, the key with one flat. Press B♭, the next key anticlockwise, then E♭ and A♭ after it.
Each step anticlockwise is a 5th down, and adds one flat.
Practice until you can say the four keys in order without looking at the circle.

The three staffs below show B♭, E♭ and A♭ major. On each one, tap up the scale from {{1}} and say each letter: the ringed {{4}} is the flat that key adds.
Practice until you can name the new flat before you tap it.
From one staff to the next the new flat is still the {{4}}, and it is the note the next flat key starts on.

The piano below shows A♭ major, four steps anticlockwise from C. Tap up the scale from {{1}} and count the black keys: one for each flat.
Then say the four flats in the order the keys added them.
Practice until the four come in order without counting round the circle.
